title: Inherited property basis - federal basics
facts: For many assets acquired from a decedent, federal income-tax basis is generally adjusted to fair market value at the date of death or another permitted valuation date, subject to statutory rules and exceptions.
This basis rule can substantially change the taxable gain or loss when inherited property is later sold.
Not every asset receives the same basis treatment; retirement accounts, income in respect of a decedent and certain other property follow different rules.
Beneficiaries should establish and retain documentation supporting the inherited asset's tax basis.
